- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or mean.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price is volatile; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion after 2–3 consecutive high prices; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if price has been above 68.0 for 3+ days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is falling, model tends to underestimate; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid “panic” underestimation.
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly down, model often overestimates; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment mismatch.
